bug_semantics: In policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles, the default fixfiles restore path and the non-destructive fixfiles relabel path run find over attacker-writable /tmp (and later /var/tmp, /var/run, and /var/lib/debug) and pass each matching pathname to a separate chcon process. A local attacker can replace an intermediate directory component with a symlink after find checks the entry but before chcon resolves the pathname. chcon --no-dereference avoids following a symlink only at the final component; it still follows swapped intermediate components, so the privileged invocation can apply an attacker-chosen SELinux label to an arbitrary target such as /etc/shadow, undermining MAC integrity.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable find-plus-chcon design predates the repository's Git history. The earliest relevant Git object, 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549, is a root snapshot titled 'initial import from svn trunk revision 2950'; its policycoreutils VERSION is 2.0.54 and the imported file already contains both vulnerable /tmp and /var/tmp commands. Because that aggregate import has no parent or SVN member commits in the validated clone, it is a history boundary rather than the smallest real BIC.
ai_marker: Unavailable for the true BIC: the BIC commit object is outside the public Git history. git cat-file -p 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549 shows only Joshua Brindle as author/committer and the SVN-import subject, with no AI trailer, but that import snapshot is not the BIC and therefore cannot supply BIC-only AI evidence.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8hc6-8f5m-vmq3 and Red Hat's https://access.redhat.com/security/cve/CVE-2026-19079 describe CWE-367: a local attacker races fixfiles relabel/restore by swapping directory components with symlinks so privileged chcon can relabel arbitrary files; GitHub reports affected and patched versions as Unknown, while Red Hat says the code has been present for many years and product versions remain subject to impact analysis.

At the vulnerable fix parent, run: git show a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679^:policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles | sed -n '230,370p'. process maps restore to 'restore Relabel'; restore's default case invokes find ... -exec chcon --no-dereference on /tmp, /var/tmp, /var/run, and /var/lib/debug. The cleanup is reached by restore without a pathname and by relabel when the user declines full /tmp deletion.

Run: git show --format=fuller --patch a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679. The direct upstream fix deletes all ten cleanup lines. Its message explicitly says find and chcon re-look up full pathnames and are subject to TOCTOU. Its sole parent is 7fd20e48504069fe1541f809de7566283f8ec7db, and the displayed parent-side hunk contains the vulnerable commands, establishing the direct closing boundary.

Run: git blame -L 288,301 a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679^ -- policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles. The final lines blame mostly to refactor 3475893b6f369b880267e920a5604174b6eaa3cd and no-dereference change 2608b4d6660af0fb8ad93f2cc144bdaab3c2afa8; neither is an origin commit. git show 3475893b6f369b880267e920a5604174b6eaa3cd shows it moved the existing cleanup into a RESTORE_MODE case, and git show 2608b4d6660af0fb8ad93f2cc144bdaab3c2afa8 shows it only added --no-dereference to already-existing find/chcon commands.

Run: git log a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679^ -L 297,297:policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles and git log --all --follow -p -S 'find /tmp' -- policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles. The line history crosses the 2017 edits, 5bd734dd7395a2f6c87546b8e7159b02544405f9 (2011 computed types/reference labels), 95e4b5c3cc37f2c62bf99428275908d7da6e4a0e (2008 expanded matching to unlabeled_t), and terminates at root import 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549, where the vulnerable find/chcon lines are added as part of the entire imported tree.

Run: git rev-list --parents --max-count=1 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549. It prints only 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549, proving the earliest vulnerable snapshot has no Git parent to test. git cat-file -p 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549 identifies it as 'initial import from svn trunk revision 2950'. Thus parent absence for a smallest real BIC cannot be verified and the aggregate cannot be decomposed from this history.

Scope expansion is separable from origin: git show 593154505a8f8c99e8f19b0aae352cd4d1d7e173 adds the same vulnerable find/chcon pattern for /var/run and /var/lib/debug in 2011, while /tmp and /var/tmp already exist in its parent. This commit enlarges the attack surface but is not the BIC for the advisory's root mechanism.

Version boundary: git show 13cd4c8960688af11ad23b4c946149015c80d549:policycoreutils/VERSION prints 2.0.54 and that same snapshot contains the vulnerable /tmp and /var/tmp commands. git rev-list -n 1 policycoreutils-3.11 resolves to 2233a23a4d4f1bf29054037babec13f30d038e65, and git show policycoreutils-3.11:policycoreutils/scripts/fixfiles still shows all vulnerable cleanup commands. git merge-base --is-ancestor a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679 policycoreutils-3.11 exits 1, and git tag --contains a556538c2d5d2583273e025b45c02651fef47679 prints no tags. The observed upstream affected span is therefore at least 2.0.54 through released 3.11; the fix landed afterward on main while policycoreutils/VERSION still read 3.11, with no fixed upstream release tag in the clone.

BIC-only marker check cannot be completed: the true pre-import SVN change has no commit object in the validated repository. The metadata of later refactors, the 2026 fix, and the non-BIC import were excluded from the AI judgment as required.
reasoning: The vulnerability is the pathname-resolution race inherent in handing find-discovered names from attacker-writable trees to privileged chcon, not the 2017 refactor or its attempted --no-dereference hardening. Both -L and -S tracing lead to an already-vulnerable whole-tree SVN import at Git root; later commits only broaden, move, or alter the same design. The immediate parent of the 2026 deletion fix is directly vulnerable, and released policycoreutils 3.11 is vulnerable, but the fix is not contained in any upstream tag. A closed AI/NOT_AI result would require the smallest real introducer's commit object and a direct parent comparison. Those objects are absent because public Git begins with SVN revision 2950 as an aggregate snapshot, so using the import author's metadata would violate the BIC-only rule. This is a genuine public-history boundary and therefore BLOCKED rather than EVIDENCE_GAP.
remaining_gap: The pre-Git SVN member revision that first added the /tmp and /var/tmp find ... -exec chcon pathname relabeling, its immediate parent tree, and that member revision's original commit object/metadata are not represented in the validated clone. Without an authoritative SVN history/dump or equivalent original commit objects, the aggregate root import cannot be decomposed, parent absence cannot be verified, and BIC-only AI evidence cannot be evaluated.
